tone_patterns: Formal, policy-oriented tone emphasizing oversight, accountability, and decision rights
Objective, descriptive language that explains governance roles without persuasive or promotional phrasing
Risk-and-control framing: governance described as mechanisms to manage conflicts, approvals, monitoring, and escalation
Process-centric wording that links committees/roles to specific governance actions (approve, oversee, monitor, report, review)
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a short contextual statement describing the overall governance model and its relationship to broader group governance
Uses repeated role blocks: each block starts with a governance body/role label followed by a compact description of responsibilities
Responsibilities are presented as a sequence of actions (e.g., decision-making, oversight, reporting, review, data collection)
Includes explicit reporting lines within the narrative (who reports to whom) as part of each role description
Mixes strategic responsibilities (policy alignment, standards alignment) with operational responsibilities (data collation, engagement tracking)
Introduces subsidiaries governance with a general statement, then explains how group strategy is cascaded and implemented locally
Uses a brief transition phrase to introduce an illustrative example, followed by short, self-contained paragraphs describing the example structure
Closes with a forward-looking paragraph describing governance evolution and periodic refresh of mandates/terms of reference
heading_patterns: Numbered subsection headings (e.g., 2.x) combining topic label with a concise descriptor
Headings use sentence case and are short, functional, and scoped (e.g., governance across a business line; governance within subsidiaries; transformation of governance model)
Subheadings are followed immediately by narrative text without additional lead-in formatting
Role/committee names appear as standalone mini-headings within the body text to segment responsibilities
table_patterns: No tables used in this excerpt; governance information is structured as repeated labeled blocks instead of tabular mapping
Implied alternative-to-table pattern: committee/role label + responsibility paragraph functions like a two-column mapping rendered in text
figure_or_diagram_patterns: No explicit figures shown in the excerpt; however, an organizational-structure description is presented in prose as if summarizing a diagram (listing governance layers from top body to working groups)
Example governance structures are described using hierarchical component lists (top-level body → committee → department → working group)
pdf_layout_patterns: Page header area contains the subsection heading and body text; page footer includes section label, page number, and report title line
Content is laid out in narrow column-like line breaks (short line lengths), suggesting a multi-column or constrained text box layout
Role blocks are visually separated by whitespace and/or line breaks, creating scannable segments
Standalone section label (e.g., 'Governance') appears near the bottom margin as a running footer element
Subsection numbering and titles are positioned prominently at the start of the page content to aid navigation
disclosure_language_patterns: Uses governance disclosure conventions: identifies governance bodies, mandates, decision scope, and reporting lines
Explicitly states separation-of-duties rationale to address conflict-of-interest risk
References alignment to external principles/standards in a neutral manner (as a governance anchor rather than a claim of performance)
Describes integration of ESG into existing decision processes (credit/investment approvals) and notes phased formalization where applicable
Uses modal/temporal qualifiers for maturity statements (e.g., evolving model, in progress, expected to be formalized) to indicate status without overcommitment
Clarifies frequency/trigger of governance activities when relevant (e.g., ad hoc meetings tied to product launches; periodic reviews)
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented through governance mechanics rather than outcomes: committees, policies, review cycles, reporting artifacts
Mentions specific governance artifacts generically (policies, terms of reference, periodic reports, ratings/reviews) as proof of process
Uses examples to illustrate subsidiary governance without turning the example into a comprehensive inventory
Shows traceability by linking responsibilities to documented processes (assessment processes, approval workflows, reporting deliverables)
section_specific_observations: Governance is communicated as a layered system: board-level oversight, management committees, functional teams, and independent specialist roles
The narrative distinguishes between group-level governance and business-line/subsidiary governance, emphasizing cascade and local implementation
Independence is highlighted via reporting lines (e.g., specialist role reporting to a committee rather than to operational teams)
The section balances structural description (who exists) with operational description (what they do and how decisions are made)
things_to_avoid_copying: Any organization, subsidiary, or committee names and acronyms
Any references to specific external initiatives or memberships as stated in the excerpt
Any descriptions that imply the reference company’s exact governance separation rationale or product/advisory context
Any mention of specific internal policies, processes, or frameworks by name
Any timing references tied to a specific year or the creation/refresh of specific forums or mandates
Any statements that could be interpreted as performance claims about ESG integration effectiveness
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Names of the organization and its asset management unit
Names of board and management committees and their acronyms
Names of subsidiaries and legal entities
Named external principles/initiatives referenced for alignment
Named internal policies, frameworks, and assessment processes
Specific year references and descriptions of governance changes introduced in that year
Mentions of specific business units and transaction labeling/recording practices tied to the reference organization
